candidates.locator: page 16, section statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, subsection A
candidates.exact_span: EPA Application Form 1 and 2C received on April 13, 2021. Additional Permit application information were received on August 26, 2021; August 20, 2021; July 29, 2021; July 20, 2021; July 8, 2021; June 30, 2021; June 21, 2021; and May 13, 2021.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Application Form 1 and 2C and supplemental submissions are identified as basis materials; different readings of which submission controls, or what discharge points, parameters, and proposed limits they describe, could change which numeric limits and monitoring parameters are treated as applicable for FY2025.

candidates.locator: page 16, section statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, subsection B
candidates.exact_span:
Citations to 40 CFR are as of December 6, 2013.
Sections 122, 124, 125, 133, 136
candidates.computation_change_reason: The incorporated 40 CFR snapshot date and cited parts determine which federal permit, effluent-guideline, and analytical-framework provisions govern; interpreting a different effective regulatory text (especially Parts 122, 133, and 136) could change enforceable limit selection and which monitoring or compliance-comparison rules apply.

candidates.locator: page 16, section statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, subsection C
candidates.exact_span:
New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Water, 20.6.4 NMAC,
effective, effective July 24, 2020.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This identifies the state water-quality standard set and effective date used in permit development; a different reading of which NMAC revision applies, or how its numeric criteria attach to the permitted discharge, could change applicable discharge limits and any standards-linked monitoring obligations for FY2025.

candidates.locator: page 16, section statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, subsection C
candidates.exact_span:
Procedures for Implementing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Permits in New
Mexico, March 15, 2012.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cited state NPDES implementation procedures are listed as permit-development authority; interpreting them differently could change which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable, including condition-triggered or procedurally conditioned monitoring for FY2025.

candidates.locator: page 16, section statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, subsection C
candidates.exact_span: State of New Mexico 303(d) List for Assessed Stream and River Reaches, 2014 - 2016.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The referenced 303(d) listing period could affect whether impaired-reach designations trigger additional effluent limits or special monitoring; different interpretations of which list vintage governs the receiving water could change both limit applicability and monitoring obligation determinations.

candidates.locator: page 16, section statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, subsection D
candidates.exact_span:
Email from Andrew Galloway, Chief Operator, Aztec Water Treatment Plant to Maria Okpala,
EPA, dated August 26, 2021; August 23, 2021; August 9, 2021; July 29, 2021; July 20, 2021;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Operator-to-agency emails are identified as administrative-record sources; if interpreted as bearing on discharge occurrence, seasonal operation, or explanations for absent results, they could change whether monitoring was required in specific periods and how missing or non-numeric monitoring evidence should be classified.
